subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding studio techniques and design problems help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
project_brief: Solve a design challenge through sketches, prototypes, final work, and critique. This is the grade 7 culminating project for "Studio Techniques and Design Problems" (ma-g7-arts-and-music-u02, unit 2), built around drawing and observation, painting or color media, print collage or mixed media, three-dimensional design, and craftsmanship and safety. Solve a design challenge through sketches, prototypes, final work, and critique. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering drawing and observation, painting or color media, print collage or mixed media, and three-dimensional design.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: drawing and observation, painting or color media, print collage or mixed media, three-dimensional design, craftsmanship and safety, and design iteration.
Meet the performance task as written: Solve a design challenge through sketches, prototypes, final work, and critique.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Solve a design challenge through sketches, prototypes, final work, and critique. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering drawing and observation, painting or color media, print collage or mixed media, and three-dimensional design.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to drawing and observation or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.
Every interpretive claim about the work is backed by a specific, quoted or cited piece of evidence from the work or its context, not a general impression.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on drawing and observation, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores painting or color media from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
